Composition rights
Public domain in the United States; Commons’ life-plus-70 claim is not supported as of 2026. Disputed: sources disagree

The 1904 publication supports US expiry. Sibelius died in 1957, so an ordinary life-plus-70 term runs through 31 December 2027. This conflicts with the file’s unqualified PD-old-70 tag. The unidentified arranger’s rights are also unestablished.

  • Commons applies PD-old-70, asserting expiry in the source country and life-plus-70 jurisdictions.
  • The standard life-plus-70 term for Sibelius’s composition runs through 31 December 2027; US publication-based expiry is separate.
[1] [7] [5] [6] [10] [8]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Inferred, not documented

Commons supplies only general PD-US-expired and PD-old-70 tags, not a recording-specific licence. The opened upstream discography documents Columbia D 12801, matrix FX 51, recorded 5 June 1925. The original acoustic commercial carrier supports an inference of publication before 1963, qualifying under rule 3’s territorial European expiry basis; no original issue catalogue or exact first-publication year was located. Publication by the end of 1925 is not established, so rule 2 is not claimed. The former 50-year European term is inferred to have expired before the 2013 extension. US sound-recording status is not established.
